reference.text: Maintain perfusion with fluids, noradrenaline and/or dobutamine, depending on individual patient need for intravascular volume, vasoconstriction or inotropy.
Do not give steroids routinely after cardiac arrest.
Avoid hypokalaemia and hyperkalaemia, which are associated with ventricular arrhythmias.
In patients with arrhythmia immediately after ROSC, follow the ALS guideline for peri-arrest arrhythmia.
In patients with arrhythmia after ROSC, treat any potential underlying causes, such as coronary occlusion or electrolyte disorders.
In patients with no arrhythmia after ROSC, do not routinely give anti-arrhythmic drug prophylaxis.
Use electroencephalography (EEG) to diagnose electrographic seizures in patients with clinical convulsions and to monitor treatment effects.
Use levetiracetam or sodium valproate as first-line antiepileptic drugs in addition to sedative drugs to treat seizures after cardiac arrest.
Attempt a wake-up trial in patients with myoclonus and benign EEG background (days after arrest).

Use short-acting sedative agents and daily sedation holds when treating post-cardiac arrest patients receiving mechanical ventilation – this may enable earlier clinical examination that is less confou
We do not recommend systematic use of neuromuscular blocking drugs in comatose post-cardiac arrest patients.
In patients with critical hypoxaemia and ARDS following cardiac arrest, the use of a neuromuscular blocker may be considered.
Patients should be nursed 30° head-up.
It is reasonable to start gastric feeding at low rates (trophic feeding) and increase as tolerated.

Given the high incidence of upper gastrointestinal ulceration in post-cardiac arrest patients and the use of anticoagulant and antiplatelet drugs both pre and post arrest, use stress ulcer prophylaxis
Anticoagulation of post-cardiac arrest patients should be individualised and be based on general ICU recommendations.

Perform a daily neurological examination in patients who are unconscious after cardiac arrest.
Clinical examination is prone to interference from sedatives, opioids or muscle relaxants. Potential confounding from residual sedation should always be considered and excluded.
Consider neurological prognostication in patients who are not awake and obeying commands (Glasgow coma scale motor score < 6) at 72 h or later after ROSC
Perform EEG from day 1 after ROSC to predict outcome and detect seizure activity in comatose patients. Routine EEG or continuous EEG monitoring may be used.

Use brain imaging studies to predict poor neurological outcome after cardiac arrest. Ensure that the images are evaluated by someone with specific experience in these studies.
Where specialist neuroradiology expertise is unavailable, consider telemedicine consultation for brain imaging interpretation.
Repeat the brain CT if the patient is unconscious at the time of prognostication (72 h–96 h after ROSC) and the first brain CT does not show signs of HIBI.
Once major confounders have been excluded, start the prognostication assessment with an accurate clinical examination (Fig. 5 ).

notes: Graded reference = statements printed with a strength and certainty in the 'Evidence informing the guidelines' section (ILCOR treatment recommendations adopted by ERC/ESICM). Concise-guideline bullets (pp2-11) are ungraded summaries; those restating a graded rec or GPS were merged into it, the rest listed as ungraded (U9+). The ungraded count (~74) is approximate: concise bullets were counted one per bullet, descriptive bullets (e.g. 'index tests are aimed at...') and the list lead-in excluded; 'we suggest' expert-opinion sentences in the evidence text were treated as restatements of concise bullets. The 100% oxygen rec is one sentence with separate grades for pre-hospital (strong, moderate) and in-hospital (strong, low); counted as two items (G1, G2). If counted as one, extracted row 14 or 15 becomes a 'split' FP. G8 (bicarbonate/calcium) and G16 (neuroprotective drugs) are 'insufficient evidence' statements labelled 'weak recommendation'; counted graded per the printed strength, but direction is not stated, so strength_ok = null (excluded): strength_ok is 28/28 evaluable (28/30 of TP). If treated as no_recommendation instead, rows 3 and 9 become 'category' FPs (tp 28, fp 4). Certainty ranges coded at the lowest level: G6 'low to moderate' -> low (row 5 ok); G16 'low- to very low' -> very_low (row 9 'low' marked not ok). Extractor emitted no ungraded rows, so ungraded_extracted_as_ungraded = 0; 2 ungraded statements were extracted as graded (FPs). G10 matched row 8; concise bullet on MCS in select populations treated as its restatement.
